statement: a new PE-ALD process, hexakis(dimethylamido)digallium with H2S plasma, deposits high-quality Ga2S3 and outperforms the thermal process with the same reactants
the PE-ALD process deposits crystalline, smooth, stoichiometric Ga2S3 already at its lowest temperature, at the highest growth per cycle, without detectable carbon or oxygen
GIWAXS shows the as-deposited Ga2S3 is cubic with a preferred [111] orientation, the (111) planes parallel to the substrate
the crystalline Ga2S3 film is less transparent than the amorphous thermal film and has a direct, narrower band gap; the wider gap of the amorphous film is attributed to oxygen
ALD's self-limiting reactions give angstrom-scale thickness control and conformal coating of complex three-dimensional substrates, but gallium sulfide by ALD has few reports
the ellipsometric thicknesses (Cauchy model) agree well with the XRR thicknesses
across the temperature window the PE-ALD growth per cycle first falls, stays flat, then rises again at the top; the thermal process follows the same trend at lower values
the higher growth per cycle of PE-ALD comes from the higher reactivity of the plasma species; the thermal values agree with Meng et al. except a lower 0.28 against 0.49 Å at 200 °C

PE-ALD shows substrate-enhanced growth at both 125 and 225 °C: about three cycles at 125 °C, and at 225 °C an S-shaped start (enhanced, then a dip, then steady), the island growth the SEM grains support
the thermal process grows linearly at 125 °C without nucleation effects, unlike the 50-cycle enhancement reported before; at 225 °C it is linear at 0.5 Å per cycle after a 20-cycle enhanced start
at 125 °C the growth per cycle saturates after a 10 s precursor dose and a 5 s H2S plasma pulse
the thermal GaSx film shows no gallium sulfide Bragg peaks in GIWAXS, only the silicon substrate, so it is amorphous, as Meng et al. found

the PE-ALD film's arc-shaped GIWAXS intensity on the Debye-Scherrer rings means preferred orientation; the integrated profile matches cubic Ga2S3 (JCPDS 43-0916), and the χ positions of (111), (220) and (311) fit (111) planes parallel to the substrate

both 150 °C films are smooth and continuous in SEM and AFM, with comparable rms roughness although the PE-ALD film is about three times thicker; at 225 °C the PE-ALD film shows islands and the thermal film none
the PE-ALD film's Ga 2p3/2 and S 2s binding energies match Ga2S3 and its S/Ga ratio means stoichiometric Ga2S3; the thermal film's far lower S/Ga is nonstoichiometric, as before

after the argon sputtering no carbon or oxygen remains in the PE-ALD film, so its surface contamination is adventitious; the thermal film keeps carbon and oxygen in its bulk, most likely from the precursor and air ageing
Meng et al.: thermal ALD from Ga2(NMe2)6 and H2S gives amorphous GaSx at 1 to 0.5 Å per cycle over 125–225 °C
Meng et al.: S/Ga between 1.0 and 1.2 over 125–200 °C, with carbon and oxygen in the bulk
